row.scenario: Clone, build and load the module without a workaround: own kernel, root and Docker on a KVM virtual machine.
row.note: A full VM with its own kernel, root, Docker and public IP. The vCPU cores are shared with other customers. Nested virtualisation is not supported on Core VPS; it is supported only on the dedicated-core Cloud VDS line.

source.quote: Contabo VPS are KVM-based virtual servers with shared vCPU cores and a fixed RAM allocation

row.scenario: There is no 2 vCPU / 16 GB Core VPS plan: the smallest Core VPS shape with 16 GB is 8 vCPU / 24 GB at $16.80, in the EU or one of eight other regions.
row.note: Six fixed Core VPS shapes from 4 vCPU / 8 GB to 18 vCPU / 96 GB, with CPU and RAM in a fixed ratio. Performance VPS and Storage VPS change the ratio, Cloud VDS goes to 24 dedicated vCores, but there is no custom sizing. Nine regions: EU (Germany), UK, three US, Singapore, Japan, India and Australia.

row.scenario: One flat $6.60 for 4 vCPU / 8 GB whether the box is busy 5% or 100% of the month; the meter never follows the work.
row.note: Prepaid terms of 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 months with one flat price per server. The 1-month term is $6.60 and the 24-month rate is $5.28, paid upfront. There is no hourly or per-second meter, so a ten-minute task costs a month and a powered-off server keeps billing.

source.quote: The price displayed is the effective monthly rate for a 24-month subscription including applicable taxes

row.scenario: No free week and no starting credit: the first invoice is paid before the server exists.
row.note: Contabo advertises no free tier, trial or signup credit on its pricing, VPS or order pages, and the cheapest 1-month plan is paid at order. Payment can be card, PayPal or bank transfer, but nothing runs before it clears.

source.quote: Provisioning takes a few minutes after payment clears.

row.scenario: Stopping at 18:00 powers the VM off: the disk and cron entries stay, the REPL and the dev server on port 3000 do not.
row.note: The panel and API offer start, stop, restart and shutdown, but no pause or hibernate. A stop is a power-off: memory and running processes are lost, the disk survives, and the monthly plan keeps billing.

source.quote: Customer Control Panel: start/stop/restart, reinstall, snapshots, VNC console, rescue system, firewall, private networking, storage extension, DNS and reverse DNS

row.scenario: A snapshot restores the disk, not the process tree; Cloud VPS 4 holds one, and it is deleted after 30 days.
row.note: Snapshots do not use the plan's disk, cannot be downloaded, and are deleted after 30 days. Cloud VPS 4 includes one slot, Cloud VPS 6 two, larger plans three. There is no memory snapshot, no fork of a running machine, and no documented way to start new servers from a snapshot. Auto Backup is a separate paid add-on with 10 daily off-server backups.

source.quote: After 30 days, the snapshots will be deleted.

row.scenario: Postgres in /var/lib survives a power-off and a reboot; the 100 GB plan disk covers the 20 GB asked for.
row.note: The whole VM disk persists with the machine, including a stop. Storage Extension adds capacity of the plan's own type, up to 1.2 TB on the top Core plan, but it is tied to that server: there is no detachable block volume. Object Storage is a separate S3-compatible product.

source.quote: Storage Extension: adds storage of the plan’s type

row.scenario: Nothing idles the VM: it stays up until you stop or cancel it, and stopping still bills.
row.note: There is no idle timer, no session lifetime and no wake-on-request, because a VPS never sleeps. A machine can run for weeks; the trade-off is that the monthly plan bills through every idle hour.

source.quote: Customer Control Panel: start/stop/restart, reinstall, snapshots, VNC console, rescue system, firewall, private networking, storage extension, DNS and reverse DNS

row.scenario: Port 3000 is reachable at the VM's public IPv4 with nothing in front of it; SSH and a VNC console are both there.
row.note: One static public IPv4 plus a /64 IPv6 subnet, any TCP or UDP port, real SSH and a browser VNC console. There is no tokenised preview link and no private URL; the firewall filters inbound traffic and leaves outbound unrestricted.

source.quote: Every server is assigned a public IPv4 address and an IPv6 subnet; further IPv4 addresses are available up to a per-product maximum.

row.scenario: Point an A record at the static IPv4 with Contabo's DNS; the certificate is yours to install and renew.
row.note: Contabo hosts DNS zones and manages PTR records for its IPs, for domains at Contabo or another registrar. It does not issue or renew TLS certificates for a VPS: you run Caddy, Certbot or a proxy. The n8n and OpenClaw images may include their own web server, but no managed certificate is documented.

source.quote: DNS zones for domains registered with Contabo or with a third-party registrar can be hosted on Contabo’s authoritative nameservers and managed self-service in the Control Panel.

row.scenario: 400 GB of dependencies costs nothing extra; Contabo reserves the right to throttle exceptional use.
row.note: Inbound and outbound traffic are unmetered, with no per-GiB price and no allowance to exceed. The catch is a fair-use policy: Contabo may throttle exceptionally high or disruptive usage, the port is 200 Mbit/s on Cloud VPS 4, and the Terms do not guarantee the bandwidth actually available. Outbound firewall rules are not offered.

source.quote: Outgoing Traffic: Unlimited — fair usage policy applies based on average server workloads.

row.scenario: The agent reads whatever is in its environment or on disk; Contabo's secret store holds only passwords and SSH keys for provisioning.
row.note: The API can store secrets of type password or ssh, reuse an SSH key across servers, and let support access a machine without emailing a password. It does not inject API keys into the machine as environment variables and has no proxy that hides a key from the agent. API users are role-scoped, not resource-scoped.

source.quote: The type of the secret. Can be `password` or `ssh`

row.scenario: Create the first VM by clicking, then drive it with the REST API, the open-source cntb CLI or Terraform.
row.note: Control panel, documented REST API with OAuth2, open-source cntb CLI, Terraform provider, cloud-init and custom images. No official Python or TypeScript SDK, no MCP server, and no PTY or file endpoints: commands and files go over SSH.

source.quote: Provisioning | Control Panel, API, or CLI

row.scenario: OpenClaw or Hermes arrives preinstalled from the 1-click list, but you finish setup over SSH; the default Ubuntu image has no coding agent.
row.note: 1-click images include OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, n8n, Paperclip AI and Ollama, installed and configured at first boot. There is no prompt API and no model credentials: you add your own keys. OpenClaw and Hermes both require SSH and their own onboarding wizard after deployment, and Contabo's support stops at the install.

source.quote: An OS image with an application preinstalled and configured at first boot.

row.scenario: Five people can share one account with role-based users, but there is no SSO, hard spend cap or usage alert documented.
row.note: Several users per account with eight predefined roles (Owner, Full Access, Technician, Billing Admin, Invoice, Abuse & Fraud, Object Storage, Object Storage r/w). API audit endpoints record changes per resource. No SAML/OIDC identity-provider login, no account-wide spend cap and no usage-alert threshold is published.

source.quote: A Contabo account can have several users. Each user holds a role that determines which areas of the account and which functions are accessible.

row.scenario: A German GmbH with a 99.9% annual network-availability promise and a DPA, but no customer-requestable SOC 2 report is published.
row.note: Contabo GmbH, Munich, founded 2003, about 300 staff and 275,000+ customers; KKR has held a majority stake since 2022. The Terms promise 99.9% annual average connectivity with no service credit, and a DPA can be created online. Location pages list SOC 1/SOC 2 Type 2 for the data centre, but Contabo publishes no trust centre or report-request route.

source.quote: The Provider will ensure that the physical connectivity of the object storage infrastructure, webspace packages, dedicated servers, virtual dedicated server and VPS is available at an annual average rate of 99.9%.
